conceptBreakdown.content:
### High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps Table

| Misconception / Trap | Biological Reality | Exam Tip / Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *"DNA Polymerase III can initiate DNA synthesis de novo without a primer."* | DNA Polymerases **CANNOT initiate synthesis de novo**. They require a free $3'\text{-OH}$ group provided by an RNA primer. | Primase synthesizes the RNA primer. |
| *"The coding strand of DNA is the template used by RNA Polymerase."* | The **TEMPLATE strand ($3' \rightarrow 5'$)** is read by RNA Polymerase. The coding strand ($5' \rightarrow 3'$) has the same sequence as the RNA. | Coding strand sequence = RNA sequence (with $T$ replaced by $U$). |
| *"DNA Polymerase I is the main replicative enzyme in E. coli."* | **DNA Polymerase III** is the main replicative enzyme. DNA Pol I removes primers ($5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease) and fills gaps. | DNA Pol I has unique $5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease activity. |
| *"All 64 codons code for amino acids in the genetic code."* | **61 codons code for amino acids**; 3 codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) are stop/nonsense codons. | 61 sense codons + 3 stop codons = 64 total. |
| *"The Lac Operon is turned ON when the repressor binds the operator."* | Binding of the repressor to the operator **turns the operon OFF**. Inducer (allolactose) causes repressor detachment to turn it ON. | Repressor binding blocks RNA Polymerase progression. |
| *"Okazaki fragments are synthesized on the leading strand."* | Okazaki fragments are short discontinuous fragments synthesized on the **LAGGING strand ($5' \rightarrow 3'$ away from fork)**. | Sealed by DNA Ligase. |
| *"Splicing removes exons and joins introns together."* | Splicing **removes non-coding INTRONS** and ligates coding EXONS together. | Catalyzed by the Spliceosome. |
| *"Radioactive ³⁵S was found in the bacterial pellet in the Hershey-Chase experiment."* | $^{35}\text{S}$ (protein) remained in the **supernatant**; radioactive $^{32}\text{P}$ (DNA) was found in the **bacterial pellet**. | Equivocal proof that DNA is genetic material. |
| *"The Wobble hypothesis allows one tRNA to bind any amino acid."* | Wobble allows one tRNA anticodon to **pair with multiple codons for the SAME amino acid** (degeneracy). | Occurs at the 3rd base of mRNA codon / 1st base of tRNA anticodon. |
| *"VNTRs used in DNA fingerprinting are protein-coding genes."* | VNTRs are **NON-CODING, repetitive DNA sequences** displaying high population polymorphism. | Inherited from parents (50% maternal, 50% paternal). |

---

### Master Glossary for Molecular Genetics

- **A-Site (Aminoacyl Site)**: Ribosomal site that receives incoming charged aminoacyl-tRNA.
- **Allolactose**: Natural inducer of the Lac operon produced by $\beta$-galactosidase cleavage of lactose.
- **Anticodon**: A 3-nucleotide sequence on tRNA that base-pairs with a complementary mRNA codon.
- **B-DNA**: Standard right-handed double helix with $10\text{ bp}$ per turn and $3.4\text{ nm}$ pitch.
- **Central Dogma**: Fundamental flow of genetic information: $\text{DNA} \rightarrow \text{RNA} \rightarrow \text{Protein}$.
- **Chargaff’s Rules**: Equivalence rules ($[\text{A}]=[\text{T}], [\text{G}]=[\text{C}]$) in double-stranded DNA.
- **Chromatosome**: Nucleosome core particle ($147\text{ bp}$) + linker DNA ($20\text{ bp}$) bound to Histone H1 ($167\text{ bp}$).-
- **Degeneracy**: Property of genetic code where one amino acid is specified by multiple codons.
- **DNA Ligase**: Enzyme that joins single-stranded phosphodiester nicks in DNA.
- **DNA Polymerase I**: Prokaryotic repair enzyme possessing unique $5' \rightarrow 3'$ exonuclease activity for primer removal.
- **DNA Polymerase III**: Main prokaryotic replicative enzyme synthesizing DNA $5' \rightarrow 3'$.
- **E-Site (Exit Site)**: Ribosomal site holding deacylated tRNA prior to release.
- **Euchromatin**: Transcriptionally active, loosely packed, lightly staining chromatin.
- **Exon**: Coding nucleotide sequence in pre-mRNA retained in mature mRNA after splicing.
- **Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs)**: HGP strategy sequencing cDNA clones corresponding to expressed mRNAs.
- **Helicase (DnaB)**: ATP-dependent enzyme that unwinds double-stranded DNA.
- **Heterochromatin**: Densely stained, transcriptionally silent, tightly packed chromatin.
- **Heterogeneous Nuclear RNA (hnRNA)**: Primary unspliced pre-mRNA transcript produced by RNA Polymerase II.
- **Histone Octamer**: Core protein complex $[(\text{H2A-H2B})_2(\text{H3-H4})_2]$ wrapping $147\text{ bp}$ DNA.
- **Intron**: Non-coding intervening sequence in eukaryotic pre-mRNA removed by splicing.
- **Lagging Strand**: Strand synthesized discontinuously in short Okazaki fragments away from fork.
- **Leading Strand**: Strand synthesized continuously $5' \rightarrow 3'$ towards the replication fork.
- **Nucleosome**: Fundamental repeating unit of chromatin ($147\text{ bp}$ DNA wrapped $1.65$ turns around histone octamer).
- **Okazaki Fragments**: Short discontinuous DNA fragments on the lagging template ($1000\text{--}2000\text{ nt}$ in bacteria).
- **Operon**: Polycistronic cluster of genes co-regulated by a single promoter and operator.
- **P-Site (Peptidyl Site)**: Ribosomal site holding tRNA carrying the nascent polypeptide.
- **Peptidyl Transferase**: Catalytic ribozyme ($23\text{S}$ rRNA in bacteria; $28\text{S}$ in eukaryotes) forming peptide bonds.
- **Pribnow Box**: Conserved $-10$ bacterial promoter sequence ($5'\text{-TATAAT-3'}$).
- **Primase (DnaG)**: RNA polymerase synthesizing short RNA primers for DNA polymerases.
- **Proofreading**: $3' \rightarrow 5'$ exonuclease activity of DNA polymerases correcting mispaired bases.
- **Reverse Transcriptase**: RNA-dependent DNA polymerase synthesizing cDNA from RNA template.
- **Ribozyme**: Catalytic RNA molecule accelerating chemical reactions ($23\text{S}$ rRNA, RNase P).
- **Semiconservative Replication**: DNA replication where daughter helix contains 1 parental strand and 1 new strand.
- **Shine-Dalgarno Sequence**: Bacterial purine-rich mRNA sequence ($5'\text{-AGGAGG-3'}$) aligning $30\text{S}$ ribosome.
- **Sigma Factor ($\sigma$)**: Transient bacterial transcription factor required for promoter recognition.
- **Spliceosome**: snRNP complex (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6) removing introns and ligating exons.
- **Telomerase**: Ribonucleoprotein reverse transcriptase maintaining linear chromosome end lengths.
- **Topoisomerase (DNA Gyrase)**: Relieves positive torsional supercoiling ahead of the replication fork.
- **Transformation**: Uptake and stable integration of naked DNA by competent bacterial cells (Griffith).
- **VNTR**: Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (minisatellites) used in DNA fingerprinting.
- **Wobble Hypothesis**: Flexible non-Watson-Crick base pairing at the 3' base of codon and 5' base of anticodon.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Essential Numerical Invariants in Molecular Genetics
conceptBreakdown.title: Essential Numerical Invariants in Molecular Genetics
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. B-DNA Dimensions: Diameter = 2.0 nm (20 Å); Pitch = 3.4 nm (34 Å); 10 bp/turn; Rise = 0.34 nm (3.4 Å).
2. Nucleosome Core: 147 bp DNA in 1.65 left-handed superhelical turns around histone octamer; Linker = 20-80 bp + H1.
3. Genetic Code: 64 total codons = 61 sense codons + 3 nonsense/stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA).
4. Human Genome Project: 3.1647 billion bp; ~20,000-25,000 genes; <2% protein coding; Dystrophin = 2.4 Mb (largest).
5. Chromosome Extremes: Chromosome 1 = 2,968 genes (most); Y Chromosome = 231 genes (fewest).
6. Meselson-Stahl Ratios: Gen 0 = 100% Heavy; Gen 1 = 100% Hybrid; Gen 2 = 50% Hybrid:50% Light; Gen 3 = 25% Hybrid:75% Light.
